I will think this through the way I always do — start from what I did last year, count the cost, and decide.

My 10.1 mu I split like this: 7 mu for the wheat-maize rotation (that is my main grain land, the soil is good there), and the other 3.1 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton I have grown on that piece for many years now — the land is a bit lighter, drains well, suits cotton better than grain.

**Wheat (winter, the 7 mu):**
Last year I used Jimai 22, the seed dealer in town said it holds up well in our dry winter. I will buy the same again — about 15 kg seed per mu. Base fertilizer I put down before sowing: one bag of compound 15-15-15 per mu, that is 50 jin, plus some diammonium phosphate. So roughly 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. Then I top-dress urea at jointing in March, about 15 kg urea per mu. Three irrigations from the well — winter water before freeze, then jointing, then grain-filling. Spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually 2 times. Rotary till before sowing. If the weather is normal I get about 500 kg per mu, that is what I have been getting.

**Maize (summer, the same 7 mu after wheat):**
Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize directly into the stubble, no-tillage with the seeder — saves time, saves money, the neighbors all do this now. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. Compound fertilizer at sowing, then top-dress urea at big trumpet stage, total about 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. Two irrigations from the well, one at sowing, one at tasseling if it is dry. Spray for borer and armyworm, 2 times. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

**Cotton (spring, the 3.1 mu):**
Bt hybrid cotton seed, the kind that resists bollworm — saves a lot of spraying. I plough the cotton land deep in spring, that piece needs it. Base fertilizer heavier on potassium because cotton needs it for the bolls — about 18 kg N, 7 kg P, 10 kg K per mu. I irrigate 4 times — at planting, budding, flowering, boll. Even with Bt I still spray 5 times — for aphids, mites, plant bugs. Cotton is more work and more cost but the price is better than grain. Yield about 280 kg seed cotton per mu, that is what my piece gives.

I do not change much from last year. The fertilizer prices are high but I would rather spend the money than lose yield — a thin crop is a disaster, extra fertilizer is just some yuan lost.
